title: RAW UNREVIEWED: trace common-stage versus final BPE boundary profiles
summary: Prospective descriptive diagnostic following1305's source-free counterexample. Replay the frozen605merge rules exactly on a separately authorized exposed scope, tracing actual token spans. For each rule M=L+R at stage j, measure M and R at the same snapshot immediately after j, then at the final snapshot. Decompose their end-boundary contrast into the common-stage contrast plus signed later-processing changes. This could locate emergence or reversal caused by later merges, without identifying morphemes, source lexical memory or the contribution to the old608score gap.
origin: Root-proposed next-selection diagnostic, with the shared-stage comparison clarified before retention. Producer reviewed relevant primary methods and mathematical scope only. No native payload, code execution or new count was accessed.

design.mechanism: An occurrence-level accounting of one fixed deterministic merge pipeline, contrasting a common intermediate snapshot with its final survivors.
design.unit: An actual token occurrence with immutable source-group identity, token type, creation-rule identity and source span. The first proposed outcome is whether its right endpoint coincides with its original complete hard-group boundary.
design.contrast: Common-stage versus final-token sampling, rather than a new parser, native morpheme assignment, arbitrary substring census, language decoder or repeat of608's model comparison.
design.prediction: The claim that a positive final M-minus-R end-profile contrast must already be present immediately after M is created can be falsified if the common-stage contrast is nonpositive but the final contrast is positive. Conversely, unchanged profiles would show that processing after this cut did not create this particular contrast; they would not identify its earlier cause.
design.scope: Prospective fixed-pipeline selection accounting only. No empirical execution or numerical result, no claim that all or a stated fraction of608is an artifact, and no confirmed native unit or meaning.
design.first_gate: Before any corpus replay, root must prospectively authorize the exact source scope and resolve whether the relevant fixed rules, base projection and boundary labels are recoverable. The next task may stop at scope or capacity; this RAW is not permission to access old source populations.
access_constraints: Use the CURRENT allowlist and current locus/purpose restrictions. The old605/608legacy91-folio population and327dependencies are not automatically admitted because they were previously exposed.
f84andf84rremain sealed; f116vremains unadmitted; f1rhas margins-only access. No blanket legacy source export, old whole-page reopening or reserve use.

A possible future route is a prospectively authorized subset of the current guarded1233complete groups, applying the old frozen rules. This would be a new scoped diagnostic, NOT an exact reproduction of608's hard-chunk population, sample, splits or score.

The old605base projection contains nine composite collapses and its own certain/uncertain separator policy. A literal22-unit panel cannot silently be equated with those base tokens. Freeze any exact permitted projection and keep its provenance and exclusions visible before replay.
Alternate readers remain separate. No image or meaning is required or authorized by this proposal.
trace_contract: Freeze the complete ordered rule sequence, initial-unit conversion and exact left-to-right nonoverlapping application semantics. Do not relearn merges, change order or repair overlap cases after seeing results.

Replay actual merges and assign each created occurrence a rule identity and original span. A literal occurrence of a string is not necessarily an occurrence created by that merge: earlier tokenization and greedy overlap matter.
Inventory train_occurrences may be overlapping pair counts, especially for L=R. Never treat them as actual token births or subtract them from final counts without a replay certificate.
Immediately after applying rule j:M=L+R, snapshot BOTH currently present M occurrences and currently present R occurrences. The comparison is not between M's stage j and R's own earlier birth stage.

Carry these occurrence identities forward. Record absorption by later rules and actual final survivors. Verify that final tokens claimed to be survivors belong to the corresponding snapshot cohort; if token-ID/spelling collisions or later creations violate that premise, retain the discrepancy rather than calling it pure selection.
Use an immutable original-group-end label. Do not substitute the next current-token identity or another changing context variable for this first boundary diagnostic.

rates_and_identity.counts: For X=M,R retain total snapshot and final token counts and the respective original-group-end counts. Also retain survival counts by that fixed endpoint label and later consuming rule.
rates_and_identity.rates: p_j(X)=endpoint_count_j(X)/total_count_j(X); p_F(X)=endpoint_count_F(X)/total_count_F(X). A zero denominator makes that rate unscorable; do not invent0or silently drop such cells.
rates_and_identity.interpretation: The first term is the COMMON-STAGE contrast. It may itself depend on earlier merges and rule j, and is not a raw-source or linguistic residual. The final two signed terms account for processing after that cut.
rates_and_identity.cohort_selection_formula: When the final cohort is exactly a subset of the stage-jcohort, let survival probabilities conditional on end/nonend be s_E,s_I. Then p_F=p_j*s_E/[p_j*s_E+(1-p_j)*s_I], where the denominator is positive. This is deterministic finite-population accounting, not a stochastic source model.
rates_and_identity.no_percentage_claim: The signed later-processing term may cancel, reverse or exceed the observed final gap. Do not convert it automatically into an artifact fraction constrained to0..100percent or divide by a near-zero gap.
rates_and_identity.aggregation: Any cohort, folio weighting, support threshold, smoothing or aggregate must be separately frozen before values are observed. Raw counts and unscorable cells remain visible even if an additional smoothed diagnostic is declared. No automatic new p-value is proposed.

decision_value.later_emergence_or_reversal: Would show that later deterministic processing creates or changes this selected boundary contrast on the chosen scope. A future writer should not be forced to explain that observed final contrast as already present in the underlying source at the common stage.
decision_value.little_or_no_later_shift: Would limit this specific later-selection explanation for the measured profiles and preserve the need to explain their common-stage contrast. It would not prove lexical storage, morphemes or absence of other representation effects.
decision_value.scope_or_capacity_stop: Would yield no empirical attribution. Do not expand pages, change projection, select favorable merges, loosen support or launch a new decoder to manufacture an answer.
decision_value.not_608_reanalysis: The endpoint-rate identity is not a decomposition of608's held cross-entropy, multi-feature primary score, null comparison or whole-form advantage. Those need different quantities and cannot be claimed from this diagnostic.

necessary_hand_controls_for_any_future_i: Self-merge A+A on AAA creates one AA occurrence, not two births; frozen left-to-right spans distinguish the unmatched final A.
1305's fixed AB->M then MC->N example separates actual M births from surviving M; do not simulate it as arbitrary literal AB substring filtering before earlier merges.
A later merge consuming M from the left or right must preserve the consumed occurrence's original endpoint label in the trace, not relabel it as a new surviving M.
A type absent at the common snapshot or final snapshot produces an explicit unscorable rate. No smoothing or convenient deletion may hide it.
